subject: How to use a text box in a Shiny App to submit full lines of R code, rather than parameters?

messages.author: 69f9f19daecaacb7
messages.subject: How to use a text box in a Shiny App to submit full lines of R code, rather than parameters?
parts:
I'm new to Shiny, so sorry in advance for any rookie mistakes!  I would like to create a Shiny App that would accept a few lines of 'real' R code, rather than parameter values, and return results (I understand that, in order for this to be possible, I may need to limit what code could be submitted).  For example, the "Shiny Text" tutorial lets the user select a dataset (e.g., rock) from a dropdown menu and then summarize that dataset.  I am wondering if there would be a way to actually submit the code "summary(rock)" in a text box and return the same results.  

Here is the code below, based on this example from Chris Beeley's "Minimal HTML UI" example, to create a simple text box, but I can't figure out how to treat the text input as 'real' R code, rather than static text.  Any help would be greatly appreciated!

index.html:

<html>

<head>
  <title>Text Box Test</title>
  <script src="shared/jquery.js" type="text/javascript"></script>
  <script src="shared/shiny.js" type="text/javascript"></script>
  <link rel="stylesheet" type="text/css" href="shared/shiny.css"/>
</head>
 
<body>

    <h1>Text Box Test</h1>

    <div id = "navigation">
    
    <p>
      <label>Text Box Test:</label><br />
      <textarea name="comment" rows = "4"
      cols = "30">Text box</textarea> 
    </p>
    
    </div>
    
    <div id = "centerDoc">
    
      <div id="textDisplay" class="shiny-text-output"></div>
      <br />
      
       
    </div>
       
</body>

</html>  

---------------------------------------------------
server.R:

library(shiny)

shinyServer(function(input, output) {


  output$textDisplay = renderText({
    input$comment})
  
  })

messages.subject: Re: How to use a text box in a Shiny App to submit full lines of R code, rather than parameters?
parts:
Hi Ross.

I have an example in the ShinyAce package that does what you're asking for: https://github.com/trestletech/shinyAce/#02-eval . It just takes in R code and evaluates it.

Much like Ramnath pointed out, though, please read the security caveat around these apps: https://github.com/trestletech/shinyAce/#security-note before deploying this on a server.

Best,
Jeff
